## Purpose

This document gives the mathematical form of each Stan model in this directory.
It is a specification, not a report.
No model here has been fit.
The correspondence to the Stan code should be exact, so this file can be checked line by line against `m0_pooled.stan` through `m7_full.stan`.

## Shared notation

Every model in the ladder predicts a single observed voltage $y_n$, for observation $n = 1, \dots, N$, where an observation is one (subject, electrode, trial, time point) combination in the pooled dataset.
Each observation carries a time $t_n$, in milliseconds relative to stimulus onset, and, where relevant, a subject index $s(n) \in \{1, \dots, S\}$, an electrode index $e(n) \in \{1, \dots, E\}$, and a trial index $r(n) \in \{1, \dots, R\}$.
The trial index is a globally unique trial id, not a within-subject trial number, since trial is specific to a subject while electrode is shared across subjects.

All models use the same fixed set of $K$ Gaussian radial basis functions of time,
$$
\phi_k(t) = \exp\left(-\frac{(t - c_k)^2}{2\ell^2}\right), \qquad k = 1, \dots, K,
$$
with centers $c_1, \dots, c_K$ and width $\ell$ fixed and supplied as data, not estimated.
Writing $\Phi_{nk} = \phi_k(t_n)$ for the $N \times K$ design matrix, every model's mean function has the form
$$
\mathbb{E}[y_n] = \sum_{k=1}^{K} w_{k}(n)\, \phi_k(t_n),
$$
for some observation-specific weight vector $w(n) = (w_1(n), \dots, w_K(n))$.
The models differ only in how $w(n)$ is built up.
Throughout, the observation-level likelihood is
$$
y_n \sim \mathcal{N}\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^{K} w_k(n)\, \phi_k(t_n),\ \sigma^2\right), \qquad \sigma \sim \text{Half-}t(3, 0, 5).
$$

Where a grouping factor contributes a deviation, it is given a non-centered parameterization.
For a factor with $G$ levels and per-basis-function standard deviation $\tau_k$, the deviation for level $g$ is
$$
b_{k,g} = \tau_k\, z_{k,g}, \qquad \tau_k \sim \text{Half-}t(3, 0, 2), \qquad z_{k,g} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1),
$$
independently across $k$ and $g$.
This is written out once here and simply referred to as "a subject deviation", "an electrode deviation", or "a trial deviation" in the sections below.

## M0: pooled

No grouping, no covariates.
A single population weight vector applies to every observation.
$$
w_k(n) = w_k^{(0)}, \qquad w_k^{(0)} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 5).
$$

## M1: subject only

Each subject has a deviation from the population weight vector.
$$
w_k(n) = w_k^{(0)} + b^{\text{subj}}_{k,\,s(n)}, \qquad w_k^{(0)} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 5),
$$
with $b^{\text{subj}}$ a subject-level deviation as defined above.

## M2: electrode only

Structurally identical to M1, with electrode as the grouping factor instead of subject.
$$
w_k(n) = w_k^{(0)} + b^{\text{elec}}_{k,\,e(n)}, \qquad w_k^{(0)} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 5).
$$

## M3: trial only

Structurally identical to M1 and M2, with trial as the grouping factor.
This is the case of the ERP waveform for one subject at one electrode varying from trial to trial around a common shape.
$$
w_k(n) = w_k^{(0)} + b^{\text{trial}}_{k,\,r(n)}, \qquad w_k^{(0)} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 5).
$$

## M4: subject and electrode, crossed

Subject and electrode deviations are added to the population weight vector independently, with no interaction term between them.
$$
w_k(n) = w_k^{(0)} + b^{\text{subj}}_{k,\,s(n)} + b^{\text{elec}}_{k,\,e(n)}, \qquad w_k^{(0)} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 5).
$$

## M5: subject, electrode, and trial, crossed

All three grouping factors contribute an additive deviation.
This is the full random-effects structure described informally as trials crossed with electrodes, nested within subjects, with no stimulus covariates yet.
$$
w_k(n) = w_k^{(0)} + b^{\text{subj}}_{k,\,s(n)} + b^{\text{elec}}_{k,\,e(n)} + b^{\text{trial}}_{k,\,r(n)}, \qquad w_k^{(0)} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 5).
$$

## M6: stimulus covariates, pooled

Orthogonal to M1 through M5.
No random deviations at all, but the population weight vector is now a linear function of two trial-level stimulus covariates, numerosity and numerosity ratio, both assumed centered and standardized before being passed to Stan.
Writing $x^{\text{num}}_n$ and $x^{\text{rat}}_n$ for the standardized covariates of observation $n$,
$$
w_k(n) = w_k^{(0)} + \gamma^{\text{num}}_k\, x^{\text{num}}_n + \gamma^{\text{rat}}_k\, x^{\text{rat}}_n,
$$
with
$$
w_k^{(0)} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 5), \qquad \gamma^{\text{num}}_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 2), \qquad \gamma^{\text{rat}}_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 2).
$$
$\gamma^{\text{num}}$ and $\gamma^{\text{rat}}$ are themselves $K$-vectors, so each says how the entire basis-function expansion, and hence the whole mean waveform shape, shifts per unit change in that covariate. This is what lets task difficulty change the shape of the mean ERP, not just its overall amplitude.

## M7: full model

M5 and M6 combined.
This is the target model for the abstract's primary analysis: a multilevel nonlinear regression in which the population-level mean waveform depends on the stimulus covariates, and subject, electrode, and trial each contribute their own additive deviation from that mean waveform.
$$
w_k(n) = w_k^{(0)} + \gamma^{\text{num}}_k\, x^{\text{num}}_n + \gamma^{\text{rat}}_k\, x^{\text{rat}}_n + b^{\text{subj}}_{k,\,s(n)} + b^{\text{elec}}_{k,\,e(n)} + b^{\text{trial}}_{k,\,r(n)},
$$
with the same priors as in M5 and M6:
$$
w_k^{(0)} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 5), \qquad \gamma^{\text{num}}_k, \gamma^{\text{rat}}_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 2),
$$
$$
b^{\text{subj}}_{k,s} = \tau^{\text{subj}}_k z^{\text{subj}}_{k,s}, \quad
b^{\text{elec}}_{k,e} = \tau^{\text{elec}}_k z^{\text{elec}}_{k,e}, \quad
b^{\text{trial}}_{k,r} = \tau^{\text{trial}}_k z^{\text{trial}}_{k,r},
$$
each $\tau \sim \text{Half-}t(3,0,2)$ and each $z \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$, independently.

In the notation of the varying-slopes-varying-intercepts analogy used to motivate this family, $w^{(0)}$ plays the role of the fixed-effect coefficients, $\gamma^{\text{num}}$ and $\gamma^{\text{rat}}$ the role of the fixed-effect covariate slopes, and $b^{\text{subj}}$, $b^{\text{elec}}$, $b^{\text{trial}}$ the role of the crossed random effects, all generalised from single numbers to $K$-vectors indexing an entire basis-function expansion rather than a single slope or intercept.

## M1+M3: subject and trial, single electrode

Not part of the M0-M7 ladder above, which treats electrode as a crossed grouping factor from M2 onward.
This variant instead fits one electrode at a time, so there is no electrode index and no electrode deviation at all; $e(n)$ is not used, and $N$, $S$, $R$ are specific to whichever single electrode's data was passed in.
Structurally it is M1 and M3 combined, additively, with no stimulus covariates.
Used for the first preliminary fits, at `POz`, `Oz`, and `Pz`, ahead of the 27 August 2026 conference presentation (see logbook).
$$
w_k(n) = w_k^{(0)} + b^{\text{subj}}_{k,\,s(n)} + b^{\text{trial}}_{k,\,r(n)}, \qquad w_k^{(0)} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 5),
$$
with $b^{\text{subj}}$ and $b^{\text{trial}}$ defined exactly as above, independently of each other.
Corresponds to `m1_3_subject_trial_single_electrode.stan`.

## What is deliberately left out

No spatial covariance between electrodes is modelled anywhere in this ladder.
Density is not included as a covariate in M6 or M7, since nothing in this repository currently maps a stimulus id to array density.
The blob (control-task) condition is not modelled here either; these models all treat the data as coming from the dot numerosity task only.
